purpose: Governance, utility and incentive source review for fourteen expansion assets under existing rules.
coder: Research assistant source-review pass; not independent review
timing_note: Work advanced while awaiting survey responses at user direction. No outcomes were used to choose decisions. Retrieval date is not a claim of historical availability; this snapshot is not a historical estimator input.

decisions.rationale: ADA ownership supplies voting weight directly or through DReps in ratification of governance actions. This is binding delegated holder governance, not just validator consensus.
Plutus execution and reference scripts incur ADA-denominated fees, including computation and memory charges. Consuming computation qualifies under the ETH utility precedent.

Fund15 was paused in January, as confirmed by the February operator update. A separate 2026 pilot opened in August with ADA onboarding and performance payments. Its grant selection and staged future rewards require assessment; the old Fund15 timetable is no longer evidence of current activity.
decisions.remaining_evidence: Verify selected pilot projects and current payments, distinguishing discretionary project selection from any qualifying rules-based usage subsidy. Do not infer inactivity of all Catalyst work from the Fund15 pause.

decisions.rationale: ACPs gather community support for changes that client implementers may schedule. This open coordination process does not give AVAX holders binding proposal execution rights; apply the ETH social-consensus precedent.
C-chain computation is charged in AVAX. This is consumption of an execution service under the ETH utility precedent.

Retro9000 states that voting is advisory and grants remain at Foundation discretion. That programme does not meet the rules-based distribution criterion; its existence alone cannot settle other AVAX incentive programmes.
decisions.remaining_evidence: Establish whether a separate active AVAX distribution programme has qualifying allocation rules; do not infer absence from discretionary grants.

decisions.rationale: The upgrade stakeholder record documents adoption through independent ecosystem participants. BCH ownership does not grant binding votes in this process; apply the BTC coordination precedent.

Current upgrade materials concern programmable capabilities, so treating BCH as only payments is insufficient. The inspected material does not settle whether BCH is required or materially privileged for a distinct service.
decisions.remaining_evidence: Trace CashTokens or contract-service consumption to BCH requirements and apply the existing utility rule consistently with the unresolved fee boundary.

decisions.rationale: The native monetary and mining description does not establish a separate active participation subsidy, nor does it rule out developer or ecosystem programmes.
decisions.remaining_evidence: Find current programme documentation sufficient to distinguish qualifying BCH rewards from mining and discretionary grants.

decisions.rationale: Dogecoin documents open node participation and community control rather than binding DOGE-weighted governance rights. Apply the BTC governance precedent.
The documented native function is transferring money. Payments and tipping are monetary use, not a separate non-governance service, under the BTC utility precedent.

The Core development fund specifies DOGE payments to contributors for qualifying releases. This is a potentially qualifying development incentive, but the 2022 announcement alone cannot establish current operation.
decisions.remaining_evidence: Confirm current fund operation and qualifying release payouts; do not code zero merely because native issuance goes to miners.

decisions.rationale: Council members have equal votes through organizational membership. HBAR ownership does not confer these council rights; governance is controlled independently of holders.
Schedule A requires HBAR payments for network services, including contract and data services. These are non-governance service consumption.
The AI bounty has HBAR-denominated prizes and published rules, but the page marks the programme closed. A remaining payout window is not evidence that payouts remain active on September 14.
decisions.remaining_evidence: Confirm outstanding qualifying distributions or another active HBAR programme; exclude historical competitions and consensus rewards.

decisions.rationale: Token documentation establishes payment and staking uses but does not identify a binding holder governance mechanism. Silence in token documentation is insufficient evidence of absence.
decisions.remaining_evidence: Locate current administration and upgrade authority documentation to establish whether holders have binding governance rights.

decisions.rationale: VRF billing privileges LINK payment through a lower premium than native-token payment. The materially privileged service criterion is met even though LINK is not the only payment option.

The current v0.2 documentation describes LINK emissions allocated by staking and participation rules to secure oracle services. This is a separable application-service security programme, analogous to the AAVE backstop precedent, rather than base-chain consensus issuance. No user-fee pass-through is assumed.
The official overview describes a collectively maintained network with no owner and voluntary software contributions. LTC ownership does not grant binding governance votes; apply the BTC precedent.
The documented native service is monetary transfer. Payment and privacy features of money do not establish a separate service-consumption role under the BTC utility precedent.
Documented miner rewards are consensus issuance and excluded from this function. This source does not establish the status of separate development or usage rewards.
decisions.remaining_evidence: Complete the current non-mining programme check before assigning a negative value.

decisions.rationale: Delegated OP voting supplies Token House rights over protocol governance. The September classification relies on protocol rights, not an assumption that historical treasury and Citizen House arrangements remain unchanged.
Execution fees are paid in ETH rather than OP. Under the ARB precedent, governance of an execution network does not itself make its governance token a service-consumption asset.
The June 2026 governance update changes grants administration. Historical OP incentive budgets and old programme announcements do not establish a currently active rules-based distribution.
decisions.remaining_evidence: Identify an active September OP programme and its distribution rules and schedule.

decisions.rationale: The operative SGP policy explicitly defines signaling votes, with default decision-making resting with core developers and the SIMD process. The on-chain programme records tallies rather than executing upgrades. Apply the existing exclusion for informal signaling; stake weighting alone does not confer binding holder authority.
SOL pays transaction fees for execution, including computation-priority fees. Apply the ETH computation-service precedent.
The documented staking rewards compensate consensus participation and are excluded. This alone cannot establish the absence of separate SOL usage or development incentives.
decisions.remaining_evidence: Check current non-consensus SOL programme rules and operating dates.

decisions.rationale: The overview lists governance voting as a SUI role, but does not establish a deployed binding holder decision process in the inspected material.
decisions.remaining_evidence: Find operative voting, execution and delegation rules or establish that the advertised mechanism is not deployed.

decisions.rationale: SUI is used for computation and storage charges. These are distinct services; sponsored or gasless transaction routes do not remove the network-level SUI service requirement.
The programme catalogue contains historical campaigns and rewards denominated in other tokens. Neither establishes an active rules-based SUI distribution on the classification date.
decisions.remaining_evidence: Verify an active SUI-denominated programme, distinguishing other-token rewards, discretionary grants, storage refunds and consensus issuance.

decisions.rationale: TRX holders elect Super Representatives through staking-derived voting rights. Elected representatives approve committee parameter changes implemented at maintenance, establishing delegated binding protocol governance.
TRX staking provides Energy and Bandwidth entitlements; TRX can also cover resource shortfalls. These rights support consumption of smart-contract execution services.
The documented representative and voter rewards distribute consensus rewards. The existing rule excludes these; separate TRX subsidy programmes are not settled by this source.
decisions.remaining_evidence: Check current non-consensus TRX distribution programmes and allocation rules.

decisions.rationale: Stellar relies on validator quorum agreement rather than ownership-weighted holder decision rights. Holding XLM does not confer the documented validator governance authority.
Soroban charges XLM for computation and ledger storage resources. Apply the existing computation and storage utility rule.
Lumens documentation establishes native-token use and ended inflation, but does not settle current ecosystem incentive programmes.
decisions.remaining_evidence: Check current XLM-denominated programmes; distinguish discretionary community grants, historical rewards and rewards in other tokens.

decisions.rationale: Amendment activation depends on trusted validator support maintained over time. Voting authority is not proportional to XRP holdings; apply the validator-coordination exclusion.

XRP reserves are required for ledger objects such as offers and trust lines. They grant access to ledger-state services beyond transferring XRP; sponsorship changes the payer rather than eliminating the reserve requirement.
Validators receive no native XRP block rewards. This does not rule out ecosystem development or usage subsidies.
decisions.remaining_evidence: Establish current qualifying XRP programme rules or documented exclusions; do not infer absence from uncompensated validation.

decisions.rationale: Coinholders approve actual grant allocations under an operating funding process. Key-holder organizations retain exceptional veto rights; the March 2026 statement documents their use. The researcher accepted constrained funding authority as qualifying governance on September 14. This establishes treasury decision rights, not protocol-upgrade control or revenue capture. The Proposed label and incomplete references in ZIP1016 are supplemented by administrator records of implementation.

researcher_review.decision: Yes—record constrained funding authority as governance
researcher_review.scope: Interpretation of constrained funding authority; not independent blind review

decisions.rationale: The native role is privacy-preserving money. Privacy of a monetary transfer is not a separate non-governance service under the BTC utility precedent.

Coinholder grants are operating, but discretionary grants are excluded from this function. Separately, Gleyo reports mainnet ZEC quest rewards since July and currently advertises ZEC rewards. A live product is not by itself a fully evidenced standing reward programme.
decisions.remaining_evidence: Inspect a current funded Gleyo quest and its allocation rules or another active ZEC incentive programme; separate user rewards from a grant to the app developer.
